Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents

Pakistan-Linked SideCopy Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry with Xeno RAT

The Hacker News
2026-06-02 15 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a spear-phishing campaign likely undertaken by the Pakistan-aligned SideCopy group targeting Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance with an open-source remote access trojan called Xeno RAT. "The campaign opens with a spear phishing delivery - a ZIP archive containing a malicious LNK file bearing a carefully crafted Pashto-language filename,"

[LLM] SideCopy LNK-via-ZIP spawning mshta.exe with remote HTA URL Delivery High
Detects the Operation XENOFISCAL initial-access stage where a Pashto-named .LNK inside a ZIP is double-clicked from explorer.exe and invokes mshta.exe with a remote URL argument to stage Xeno RAT. The parent=explorer + child=mshta + remote-URL combination is the article's specific entry pattern. Rationale: Article-specific: SideCopy's Operation XENOFISCAL chain explicitly states the .LNK opens via mshta.exe to fetch a remote .hta. The parent=explorer/archiver + child=mshta + URL arg is a high-signal triad and matches the Seqrite report's step 1. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1008/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1218.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","winrar.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winzip64.exe","winzip32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\winrar.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\7zg.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\7zfm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\winzip64.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\winzip32.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
title: Mshta Spawned by Explorer/Archiver with Remote URL
id: 6f3d4e08-2c4b-4a92-b6e8-2c4c3d2a7c61
description: Detects mshta.exe spawned by explorer.exe or a common archive utility with an http(s) URL argument, matching the SideCopy Operation XENOFISCAL LNK-in-ZIP loader.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/pakistan-linked-sidecopy-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/02
tags:
  - attack.t1218.005
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\winrar.exe'
      - '\7zg.exe'
      - '\7zfm.exe'
      - '\winzip64.exe'
      - '\winzip32.exe'
  selection_arg:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - '.hta'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) (@Image:(*\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\Mshta.exe) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\Mshta.exe)) (@ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.EXE OR *\\winrar.exe OR *\\WinRAR.exe OR *\\7zG.exe OR *\\7zFM.exe OR *\\winzip64.exe OR *\\winzip32.exe) OR @ParentProcessName:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.EXE OR *\\winrar.exe OR *\\WinRAR.exe OR *\\7zG.exe OR *\\7zFM.exe)) (@CommandLine:(*http\:* OR *https\:* OR *.hta*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\mshta\.exe$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(explorer\.exe|winrar\.exe|7zG\.exe|7zFM\.exe|winzip64\.exe|winzip32\.exe)$/i
| regex("(?i)(https?://|\\.hta)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

[LLM] Xeno RAT staging — mshta/wscript fetching HTA from abimj.edu.af Delivery High
Detects the second-stage delivery in Operation XENOFISCAL where mshta.exe (or other LOLBins) reaches out to the compromised Afghan education domain abimj.edu.af to retrieve the obfuscated JavaScript HTA dropper. Pivots on the article's named C2/staging domain in both process command-line and network telemetry. Rationale: abimj.edu.af is explicitly named by Seqrite as the compromised Afghan education domain that hosts the HTA payload. A single fully-qualified-domain match is high-fidelity, near-zero-FP, and covers DNS, proxy, and EDR pivot points. Cross-checked against MITRE G1008 (Transparent Tribe/SideCopy) profile. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1008/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/pakistan-linked-sidecopy-targets.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1218.005 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let staging_domain = "abimj.edu.af";
let proc = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has staging_domain or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has staging_domain
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="Process";
let net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where RemoteUrl has staging_domain

[LLM] Xeno RAT Registry Run-key persistence impersonating Microsoft Edge Installation Medium
Detects the SideCopy persistence trick where a Run-key value is named to mimic Microsoft Edge (e.g. 'MicrosoftEdge', 'EdgeUpdate') but the value's data points to a non-Edge path such as %AppData%, %ProgramData%, %Public%, or %Temp%. This is the article's described Registry-based persistence mechanism for Xeno RAT 1.8.7. Rationale: Article-specific persistence mechanism: 'Registry-based persistence by mimicking Microsoft Edge.' Edge legitimately writes Run keys but always from %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft\Edge\ or the EdgeUpdate service — anchoring on Edge-named Run value + non-Edge path delivers a tight, high-fidelity hunt for the named persistence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/005/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueName has_any ("Edge","msedge","MicrosoftEdge","EdgeUpdate")
| where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Temp\", ".hta", "mshta", "rundll32", "regsvr32", "wscript", "cscript")
| where RegistryValueData !has @"\Program Files\Microsoft\Edge\"
     and RegistryValueData !has @"\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\"
     and RegistryValueData !has @"\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","setup.exe","msiexec.exe","microsoftedgeupdate.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeySet","RegistryValueCreate","RegistryKeyCreate")
| where RegistryKey has @"\CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValue has_any ("Edge","msedge","MicrosoftEdge","EdgeUpdate")
| where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Temp\", ".hta", "mshta", "rundll32", "regsvr32", "wscript", "cscript")
| where RegistryValueData !has @"\Program Files\Microsoft\Edge\"
     and RegistryValueData !has @"\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\"
     and RegistryValueData !has @"\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith "msedge.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith "MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith "setup.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith "msiexec.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

[LLM] SideCopy Xeno RAT C2 egress to 185.235.137.106 / 103.132.98.224 / 103.132.98.226 Command & Control High
Detects outbound TCP connections to the three named Xeno RAT C2 IPs from any process. Pairs the IP match with the initiating process so analysts can immediately see whether the caller is mshta, an unsigned DLL host, or a renamed payload — the article confirms Xeno RAT 1.8.7 uses raw TCP for operator commands. Rationale: All three IPs are explicitly published in the pre-extracted IOC bundle for this article. A bare three-IP match is the cheapest, highest-confidence C2 signal we can ship; pairing it with InitiatingProcess gives the analyst the binary to triage in one click. Cross-checked the IOC bundle against MITRE G1008 (SideCopy/Transparent Tribe). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1008/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0134/
ATT&CKT1571 T1095 T1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteIP in ("185.235.137.106","103.132.98.224","103.132.98.226")
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, LocalIP, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
     | where DestinationIP in ("185.235.137.106","103.132.98.224","103.132.98.226")
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction),
  (ImNetworkSession
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
     | where DstIpAddr in ("185.235.137.106","103.132.98.224","103.132.98.226")
     | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkApplicationProtocol, EventVendor, EventProduct, DvcAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Known Xeno RAT 1.8.7 (Operation XENOFISCAL) hash execution or drop Installation High
Atomic file-hash detection for the eight SHA256 and one MD5 published for the SideCopy XENOFISCAL campaign. Covers process execution, file write, and DLL image load surfaces so the rule fires whether the DLL-based Xeno loader is on disk, in memory as a module, or executed directly. Rationale: All nine hashes are published in the pre-extracted IOC bundle for this article and refer to the Xeno RAT loader, decoy doc, and side-loaded DLL components. Hashes are atomic, low-FP, and three-table coverage (process / file write / image load) catches the DLL-based-loader execution path the article describes. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1008/ • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1100/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1574.002

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args Installation High
schtasks.exe /create or Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler EventID 4698 with LOLBin actions.
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64","\Users\Public","\AppData\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","cmd.exe","rundll32","-enc","FromBase64",
                              "\Users\Public", "\AppData\")

          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.initial-access

            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'

// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("194b912c242604d6f9a79369f22338c58a13ce0cc2ed280ce505075808bc2f14", "3b4194bdfe40d94031a94b30397ffd8a4b09d0a4057668e897b8bdcd1703dd01", "df9173a28c0b0b878c10a53d35cd7ce6f6ed66d207b6b7c4ff723721f1c027ab", "a63e90ee57a1f213a8fe76ef1a6cff5ae9ed7ebceda258431533825e648c0c67", "5833917bd137804f5a021d2cb37adfe5c4b7b67dbb06d59c3b9c5cf393835e45", "99127c8c67d90e2776beeb85281f9c68399bf4567b07a6b638d68b760212e88d", "8f2d979ef33b2900351c94c7335275a9342c75189e1a901998e90a539e944a1a", "0019212f25eb04bbb33bb194879c095265db7855d6003bdd777cf0cbb90eb772", "9ae3d785486022af82ea92e51b26e3f55c1bba88a7be2ad9790f4240e8499d14", "3563518ef8389c7c7ac2a80984a2c4cd") or SHA1 in~ ("194b912c242604d6f9a79369f22338c58a13ce0cc2ed280ce505075808bc2f14", "3b4194bdfe40d94031a94b30397ffd8a4b09d0a4057668e897b8bdcd1703dd01", "df9173a28c0b0b878c10a53d35cd7ce6f6ed66d207b6b7c4ff723721f1c027ab", "a63e90ee57a1f213a8fe76ef1a6cff5ae9ed7ebceda258431533825e648c0c67", "5833917bd137804f5a021d2cb37adfe5c4b7b67dbb06d59c3b9c5cf393835e45", "99127c8c67d90e2776beeb85281f9c68399bf4567b07a6b638d68b760212e88d", "8f2d979ef33b2900351c94c7335275a9342c75189e1a901998e90a539e944a1a", "0019212f25eb04bbb33bb194879c095265db7855d6003bdd777cf0cbb90eb772", "9ae3d785486022af82ea92e51b26e3f55c1bba88a7be2ad9790f4240e8499d14", "3563518ef8389c7c7ac2a80984a2c4cd") or MD5 in~ ("194b912c242604d6f9a79369f22338c58a13ce0cc2ed280ce505075808bc2f14", "3b4194bdfe40d94031a94b30397ffd8a4b09d0a4057668e897b8bdcd1703dd01", "df9173a28c0b0b878c10a53d35cd7ce6f6ed66d207b6b7c4ff723721f1c027ab", "a63e90ee57a1f213a8fe76ef1a6cff5ae9ed7ebceda258431533825e648c0c67", "5833917bd137804f5a021d2cb37adfe5c4b7b67dbb06d59c3b9c5cf393835e45", "99127c8c67d90e2776beeb85281f9c68399bf4567b07a6b638d68b760212e88d", "8f2d979ef33b2900351c94c7335275a9342c75189e1a901998e90a539e944a1a", "0019212f25eb04bbb33bb194879c095265db7855d6003bdd777cf0cbb90eb772", "9ae3d785486022af82ea92e51b26e3f55c1bba88a7be2ad9790f4240e8499d14", "3563518ef8389c7c7ac2a80984a2c4cd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents

// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["194b912c242604d6f9a79369f22338c58a13ce0cc2ed280ce505075808bc2f14", "3b4194bdfe40d94031a94b30397ffd8a4b09d0a4057668e897b8bdcd1703dd01", "df9173a28c0b0b878c10a53d35cd7ce6f6ed66d207b6b7c4ff723721f1c027ab", "a63e90ee57a1f213a8fe76ef1a6cff5ae9ed7ebceda258431533825e648c0c67", "5833917bd137804f5a021d2cb37adfe5c4b7b67dbb06d59c3b9c5cf393835e45", "99127c8c67d90e2776beeb85281f9c68399bf4567b07a6b638d68b760212e88d", "8f2d979ef33b2900351c94c7335275a9342c75189e1a901998e90a539e944a1a", "0019212f25eb04bbb33bb194879c095265db7855d6003bdd777cf0cbb90eb772", "9ae3d785486022af82ea92e51b26e3f55c1bba88a7be2ad9790f4240e8499d14", "3563518ef8389c7c7ac2a80984a2c4cd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)

                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DriveSurge zTDS loader script injection (t.js?site=<id>) outbound Delivery High
Hunts for browsers fetching the DriveSurge JavaScript loader served from compromised sites via the 't.js?site=<id>' URI pattern, or contacting the campaign's injection/TDS domains. This is the earliest visible step of the kill chain before any payload is served. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-unique 't.js?site=<id>' loader URI pattern plus the 8 injection/TDS hostnames and 4 IPs explicitly listed in the article and SilentPush IOC drop. Restricting to browser-initiated traffic strips out scanner/researcher noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1189/
ATT&CKT1189 T1583.008

| where (RemoteUrl has "t.js?site=")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("beacontrace.bond","check.first-node.rocks","cptoptious.com","webgleam.info","banerpanel.live","testio.ecartdev.com","newtdsone.shop","captioto.com","ztds.info")
   or RemoteIP in ("91.92.240.127","46.226.166.57","147.45.42.200","147.45.42.205")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

let DriveSurgeIPs = dynamic(["91.92.240.127","46.226.166.57","147.45.42.200","147.45.42.205"]);
ImWebSession

    or HttpHostName has_any (DriveSurgeDomains)
    or DstIpAddr in (DriveSurgeIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, HttpHostName, Url, DstIpAddr, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FakeUpdates 'Browser Update.exe' drop from ZIP in user-writable path Installation High
Detects execution of the campaign's fake Firefox/Chrome/etc. installer binary 'Browser Update.exe' or its sibling DLLs from Downloads/%TEMP%, especially when the parent is a browser or archive utility. Targets the FakeUpdates payload stage described in the Silent Push report. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'Browser Update.exe' as the fake-Firefox payload bundled in a ZIP with DLLs, and provides four SHA256s for the campaign's stagers. Filename + hash + user-writable-path are all article-grounded high-fidelity anchors. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/005/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let CampaignHashes = dynamic(["90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc","7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d","8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a","e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "Browser Update.exe"
    or SHA256 in (CampaignHashes)
    or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (CampaignHashes)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winrar.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignHashes = dynamic(["90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc","7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d","8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a","e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a"]);
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName endswith "Browser Update.exe"
    or TargetProcessName endswith "Browser Update.exe"
    or SHA256 in (CampaignHashes)

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] ClickFix PowerShell pasted from browser-originated clipboard (Run dialog chain) Exploitation High
Detects the ClickFix social-engineering chain: an explorer.exe (Win+R Run dialog) or browser process spawning powershell.exe / cmd.exe with telltale ClickFix payload patterns (mshta-fetched JS, curl/iex/IWR pipelines) that the victim pasted from a malicious 'verification' page. Pivots on the article's PowerShell-execution Phase 3 description. Rationale: Article Phase 3 explicitly cites 'powershell.exe spawned from explorer.exe or a browser parent shortly after a clipboard write' as the ClickFix execution shape, and the campaign's PowerShell payloads reach back to the 8 named injection/TDS domains in the article. The parent + child + cmdline-substring triad is exactly the high-fidelity pivot the BluRaven 'pattern-process-tree' anchor calls for. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/

[LLM] DriveSurge campaign IP beaconing post-payload execution Command & Control High
Detects outbound TCP/HTTP connections to the four DriveSurge C2/TDS IPs (91.92.240.127, 46.226.166.57, 147.45.42.200, 147.45.42.205) initiated by non-browser processes — i.e. the post-install beacon shape that follows the FakeUpdate or ClickFix execution stage. Rationale: Four campaign IPs are explicitly provided as zTDS/payload infrastructure. Excluding browser-initiated traffic isolates the post-execution beacon (loader/stealer/CS) from the upstream loader fetch already covered by UC #1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105

| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe","yandex.exe","safari.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc

| where DstIpAddr in (CampaignIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] macOS ClickFix clipboard-hijack: Terminal/osascript shell exec from browser context Exploitation Medium
Detects the macOS variant of ClickFix where a 'verification' page hijacks the clipboard and tricks the user into pasting an attacker-supplied curl/bash one-liner into Terminal. Targets Defender for Endpoint macOS process telemetry — Terminal or osascript spawning bash/sh/zsh with curl + pipe-to-sh sequences shortly after a browser was active. Rationale: Article Phase 5 explicitly calls out the macOS ClickFix variant 'hijacks the clipboard' and Phase 3 lists 'osascript spawned from explorer.exe or a browser parent shortly after a clipboard write' plus 'curl, base64, or sh -c sequences' as the detection hint. Parent (browser/Terminal) + child (shell) + command-substring (curl|sh, base64 -d, do shell script) is the high-fidelity triad. Cross-checked against: • https://www.silentpush.com/blog/drivesurge/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1204.004 T1115
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceId in ((DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform == "macOS" | distinct DeviceId))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Terminal","iTerm2","osascript","Safari","Google Chrome","firefox","Brave Browser","Microsoft Edge")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","zsh","curl","osascript","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl -s","curl -sS","curl -fsSL","| sh","| bash","| zsh","base64 -d","base64 --decode","do shell script","eval $(curl")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_all ("curl","http","|")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "mac" or DvcOs has "darwin"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Terminal","iTerm2","osascript","Safari","Google Chrome","firefox","Brave Browser","Microsoft Edge")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","zsh","curl","osascript","wget")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl -s","curl -sS","curl -fsSL","| sh","| bash","| zsh","base64 -d","base64 --decode","do shell script","eval $(curl")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "curl" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "http" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "|")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or SHA1 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or MD5 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or SHA1 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a") or MD5 in~ ("90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["90aecb370dfb1a99a1f7de0a9c6842ab1b664521fddea16b0ec9a91f322646fc", "7aa15de93cf85729ddf970e8d7897f69ece3ca29608f73e784a9ba40c9cea18d", "8ecc7108cd679316bf5900e84f19b256dc399902cdede646493f502ac872cc1a", "e1ce4e6222396a58d13dddfe64c1dd21f1632bcbe11d1867d44bab4fc646883a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Miasma Supply Chain Attack Compromises Red Hat npm Packages with Credential-Stealing Worm

The Hacker NewsBleepingComputerStepSecurity
2026-06-01 11 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Several packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope were found to carry malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install. The affected versions span multiple packages across the RedHat Cloud Services frontend ecosystem. The payload is a sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI tokens

[LLM] npm preinstall executing oversized index.js from @redhat-cloud-services scope Installation High
Hunts for the Miasma supply-chain payload entry point: npm install spawning `node index.js` for a package under `node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services/`, where index.js is unusually large (~4.2 MB). Legit libraries in this scope ship tiny CJS/ESM entry files; a multi-MB index.js is the immediate static anomaly the researchers flagged. Rationale: Anchors on three article-specific facts: the `@redhat-cloud-services` npm scope, an `index.js` entrypoint at npm install time, and the 4.2 MB index size (using 512 KB as a conservative anomaly floor — legit JS entry files are typically <50 KB). Parent-process filter ensures we catch the preinstall-hook execution path, not arbitrary node invocations. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/javascript-clients/issues/492 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/frontend-components/issues/2329
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007

let LookbackDays = 14d;
let ScopePath = @"node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\";
let ScopePathNix = "node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services/";
let HeavyDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where (FolderPath has ScopePath or FolderPath has ScopePathNix)
    | where FileName =~ "index.js"
    | where FileSize > 524288
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm","npm.cmd","node.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services" or ProcessCommandLine has ScopePath or ProcessCommandLine has ScopePathNix
| join kind=inner HeavyDrop on DeviceId
| where DropTime between (Timestamp - 5m .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, IndexPath = FolderPath1, IndexSize = FileSize, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let ScopeWin = @"node_modules\@redhat-cloud-services\";
let ScopeNix = "node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services/";
let HeavyDrop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated" or EventType == "FileModified"
    | where (TargetFilePath has ScopeWin or TargetFilePath has ScopeNix)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "index.js"
    | where TargetFileSize > 524288
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","npm-cli.js","yarn","pnpm","npm.cmd","node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services"
| join kind=inner HeavyDrop on DvcHostname

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Node-driven Bun runtime download from oven-sh GitHub Releases during npm install Delivery High
Detects the Miasma Stage-3 `_b` downloader: the malicious package's node process fetches the legitimate Bun v1.3.13 binary from the official oven-sh GitHub Releases CDN, drops it under /tmp, and uses it to execute Stage-4. The Bun-from-GitHub-during-npm-install pattern is the smoking gun — legit npm scripts almost never pull alt runtimes mid-install. Rationale: Article explicitly names Bun v1.3.13 fetched from the official GitHub releases CDN by the `_b` Stage-3 downloader, then dropped under /tmp/<random>/. Pairing the node-initiated network fetch with a /tmp Bun binary drop in a short window eliminates dev-machine FPs where engineers install Bun manually via curl. ImWebSession used on Sentinel side (HttpHostName + Url are real columns, unlike SrcProcessName which was the prior error). Cross-checked against: • https://bun.sh/docs/installation • https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.3.13
ATT&CKT1105 T1027 T1140

    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DropPath = FolderPath, DropFile = FileName, DropSHA256 = SHA256, DropInitiator = InitiatingProcessFileName, DropInitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents

   and RemoteUrl has "bun-v1.3.13"

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Stage-4 implant written to /tmp/p<random>.js and executed by freshly dropped Bun binary Exploitation High
Detects the Miasma Stage-4 execution handoff: a randomly-named JS file at `/tmp/p<random>.js` (the decrypted 634 KB obfuscator.io payload) being executed by the Bun binary that the downloader just dropped under /tmp. This parent→child shape is article-specific and impossible to legitimately reproduce in normal CI. Rationale: Article explicitly states `_p` is written to `/tmp/p<random>.js` and executed via the freshly downloaded Bun binary — both paths are pinned to /tmp, parent is node, child is bun, and the JS filename matches `p[a-z0-9]+.js`. Regex on the cmdline anchors the random-naming convention without over-fitting on a specific suffix.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1140 T1036.005

   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\\Temp\\p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
