[LLM] CI runner reading cloud-provider credential env files immediately after npm install Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Miasma credential-harvest stage: the Stage-4 implant enumerates GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm, and CircleCI credential locations. Detects node/bun processes reading the well-known credential paths within minutes of an npm install on the same host, which is highly anomalous on CI runners. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact secret stores the implant harvests (GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, CircleCI). I include the canonical credential file paths for each + GitHub Actions runner internals (`_runner_file_commands`, `RUNNER_TOKEN`). DistinctTargets >= 2 cuts noise from a single legitimate AWS CLI in a JS test. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or SHA1 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or MD5 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or SHA1 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e") or MD5 in~ ("ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709", "4c26cf9791bce1bfd4b84eba80ce2754", "ec514c074caf0ffdce6c66a0e95753d8", "5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Multiple Dashlane users have been locked out of their accounts following brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Dashlane brute-force lockout / new-device verification emails to corporate mailboxes (May-Jun 2026 campaign)
[LLM] Dashlane brute-force lockout / new-device verification emails to corporate mailboxes (May-Jun 2026 campaign) Actions on Objectives Medium
Identifies corporate users who received legitimate Dashlane suspension or new-device verification emails during the May 31 - Jun 1 2026 brute-force campaign. These mails (e.g. 'Your account has been temporarily suspended for security reasons...didn't enter the correct token after several tries') mean the attacker reached the account-targeting stage at Dashlane's auth tier for that user; the SOC should proactively rotate the user's master password, revoke active sessions, and watch the user for follow-on phishing. Rationale: Anchors on article-specific signals: Dashlane sender domain (dashlane.com / mail.dashlane.com), May 31 2026 campaign start window per Dashlane status page, and Dashlane's exact suspension-mail phrasing reported by The Register / Help Net Security ('Your account has been temporarily suspended ... didn't enter the correct token after several tries'). Aggregating per-recipient with EmailCount >= 2 raises confidence that the user was actively targeted (one-off legit new-device setup will normally produce one mail, not several). Cross-checked Dashlane status page (status.dashlane.com), The Register and Help Net Security write-ups confirming KR/RU source IPs and email phrasing; skipped image fetch since the in-article notice.jpeg is a UI screenshot of the same Dashlane email already quoted in the body. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/06/01/password-manager-dashlane-suspends-customer-accounts-amid-brute-force-attacks/5248991 • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/01/dashlane-brute-force-attack-user-accounts/ • https://cyberinsider.com/dashlane-hit-by-brute-force-campaign-triggering-account-suspensions/ • https://status.dashlane.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/
ATT&CKT1110 T1110.003 T1078.004
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
let CampaignStart = datetime(2026-05-31T00:00:00Z);
let DashlaneDomains = dynamic(["dashlane.com","mail.dashlane.com","notify.dashlane.com"]);
let DashlaneSubjectTokens = dynamic(["suspended","verification code","new device","verify your","sign-in attempt","temporarily suspended","didn't enter the correct token"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > CampaignStart - 1d and Timestamp < CampaignStart + 14d
| where SenderFromDomain in~ (DashlaneDomains)
   or SenderMailFromDomain in~ (DashlaneDomains)
| where Subject has_any (DashlaneSubjectTokens)
   or Subject has_any ("Dashlane", "new sign-in")
| where DeliveryAction in~ ("Delivered", "DeliveredAsSpam")
| summarize EmailCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            Subjects  = make_set(Subject, 10),
            Senders   = make_set(SenderFromAddress, 5),
            MsgIds    = make_set(NetworkMessageId, 10)
        by RecipientEmailAddress
| extend WindowHours = datetime_diff('hour', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| extend RiskNote = case(
        EmailCount >= 3, "3+ Dashlane brute-force notifications - very likely targeted",
        EmailCount == 2, "2 Dashlane notifications - investigate user",
        "single Dashlane notification - confirm with user")
| order by EmailCount desc, LastSeen desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — WordPress malware campaign hides payloads in Steam profiles
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WordPress backdoor authentication via tEcaKKXEsb cookie or new_code POST parameter · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] WordPress server-side outbound to Steam Community (C2-via-profile-comments) · [LLM] WordPress server / browser egress to hello-mywordl[.]info (stage-2 JS loader) · [LLM] PHP / web-runtime process spawning cURL with SSL verification disabled · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] WordPress server-side outbound to Steam Community (C2-via-profile-comments) Command & Control Medium
Hunts for WordPress/web-server hosts making outbound calls to steamcommunity.com — the GoDaddy-tracked campaign uses Steam profile comments as a dead-drop C2 (invisible Unicode encodes a stage-2 URL). Web servers should never legitimately need to read Steam profiles. Rationale: Anchored on the article's central TTP — server-side fetch of Steam profile comments as the C2 channel. Web servers (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) reaching steamcommunity.com is the smell; legitimate user-driven Steam browsing happens from workstations, never from the server-side LAMP/LEMP runtime. Domain confirmed in BleepingComputer body and GoDaddy report referenced in article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.godaddy.com/resources/news/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/001/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("steamcommunity.com","store.steampowered.com") or RemoteUrl matches regex @"steamcommunity\.com/(id|profiles)/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebSvcProcs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name has_any (SteamHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Query=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Src="DnsEvents"),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (SteamHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Src="ImDnsActivity"),
(ImNetworkSession

  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=coalesce(Url,DstHostname), QueryType="NetSession", Src="ImNetworkSession"),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csReferer has "steamcommunity.com" or csUriQuery has "steamcommunity.com"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Query=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), QueryType="IIS", Src="W3CIISLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] WordPress backdoor authentication via tEcaKKXEsb cookie or new_code POST parameter Installation High
Detects inbound HTTP POST requests containing the campaign-specific authentication cookie 'tEcaKKXEsb' or the 'new_code' parameter the backdoor uses to ingest base64-encoded PHP. Both strings are unique to this GoDaddy-reported family and survive obfuscation rotation. Rationale: Two needle-in-haystack strings called out verbatim by GoDaddy and quoted in the article — 'tEcaKKXEsb' cookie and 'new_code' POST parameter — that have no benign reason to appear in inbound traffic. Any single hit is investigable. Defender/Falcon left empty because EDR doesn't reliably capture L7 request bodies/cookies; these only surface in web-tier / WAF telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001

  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"

  | project TimeGenerated, Host=CsHost, ClientIP=CIp, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Query=CsUriQuery, Cookie, UA=UserAgent, Status=ScStatus, Src="AppServiceHTTPLogs"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestCookies has "tEcaKKXEsb" or RequestURL has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Query=RequestURL, Cookie=RequestCookies, UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), Src="CommonSecurityLog"),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriQuery has "new_code=" or csUriStem has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Query=csUriQuery, Cookie="<not-logged>", UA=csUserAgent, Status=tostring(scStatus), Src="W3CIISLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] WordPress server / browser egress to hello-mywordl[.]info (stage-2 JS loader) Command & Control High
Alerts on any DNS/HTTP egress to hello-mywordl[.]info — the article's named stage-2 domain serving the injected JavaScript disguised as asahi-jquery-min-bundle / lodash.core.min.js. Catches both the WP server fetching the payload and end-user browsers loading the injected library on infected sites. Rationale: Single named domain IOC (hello-mywordl[.]info) called out verbatim by BleepingComputer / GoDaddy as the stage-2 loader URL. A multi-source union (DNS + L7 web + WAF) catches both the WP origin pulling the payload and end-user clients loading the injected JS. No legitimate use of this domain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1059.007
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomain)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Src="NetworkEvent"),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","InboundConnectionAccepted") and RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomain)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Src="DeviceEvent")
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomain = dynamic(["hello-mywordl.info"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Type="DNS", Src="DnsEvents"),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Type="DNS", Src="ImDnsActivity"),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has_any (BadDomain) or HttpHostName has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(Url,HttpHostName), Type="Web", Src="ImWebSession"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomain) or RequestURL has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(RequestURL,DestinationHostName), Type="CEF", Src="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PHP / web-runtime process spawning cURL with SSL verification disabled Command & Control Medium
Hunts for web-server processes (php-fpm, php-cgi, apache2, nginx, w3wp) invoking curl with -k / --insecure / CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=false. The article explicitly names disabled SSL verification in cURL as a campaign tell — used to talk to Steam and to hello-mywordl[.]info without TLS pinning hassle. Rationale: The article explicitly lists 'disabled SSL verification in cURL requests' as an IOC. Pairing that flag with a web-runtime parent (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) is high-signal — sysadmins debugging with curl -k do so from interactive shells, not from PHP-FPM workers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let WebSvcParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebSvcParents)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s-k\b|--insecure\b|--no-check-certificate\b|VERIFYPEER\s*=\s*(0|false))"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebSvcParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (WebSvcParents) or ActingProcessName has_any (WebSvcParents)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","curl.exe","wget")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s-k\b|--insecure\b|--no-check-certificate\b|VERIFYPEER\s*=\s*(0|false))"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP / Web-Runtime Spawning cURL with SSL Verification Disabled
id: f3b8d2a4-1c6e-49a7-9b1f-2c8d4a6e7711
description: Web-server processes (php-fpm, apache2, nginx, w3wp) spawning curl with -k/--insecure — matches the GoDaddy-reported WordPress Steam-comment campaign which disables TLS verification when fetching its stage-2 loader.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1573
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-cgi'
      - '/php'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '\curl.exe'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -k '
      - ' --insecure'
      - 'VERIFYPEER=0'
      - 'VERIFYPEER=false'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_args
level: medium
(source:linux.auditd @process.parent.name:(php-fpm OR php OR php-cgi OR apache2 OR httpd OR nginx) @process.name:curl @process.command_line:(*" -k "* OR *"--insecure"* OR *VERIFYPEER=0* OR *VERIFYPEER=false*)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR *\w3wp.exe) @Image:(*\curl.exe OR *\CURL.EXE) @CommandLine:(*" -k "* OR *"--insecure"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/curl(\.exe)?$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx|w3wp\.exe)$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\s-k\\b|--insecure|VERIFYPEER\\s*=\\s*(0|false))", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

| sort - count

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or SHA1 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or MD5 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or SHA1 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or MD5 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner (CVE-2026-47413) Exploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-47413 primitive: a POST to /workspaces/{id}/members whose body contains role=owner, returning 201. The vulnerable endpoint accepts owner grants from any member-tier token, so any successful 201 on this path warrants review against the caller's known role. Rationale: Detection is grounded in the exact route the advisory names (`POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members` at workspaces.py:92-101) and the documented response status 201. No external corroboration beyond the GHSA advisory itself; the CVE is freshly published and there are no third-party write-ups yet. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8g2p-pqm3-fcfh
ATT&CKT1068 T1078.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting does not natively ingest praisonai-platform HTTP logs.
// If the app is fronted by an MDA-monitored proxy that ships to CloudAppEvents, pivot there:
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("HttpRequest","ApiCall")
| where RawEventData has "/workspaces/" and RawEventData has "/members"
| where RawEventData has_any ("\"role\":\"owner\"","role=owner")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, UserAgent, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Path 1 — Azure App Service hosting praisonai-platform
let AppHits = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
    | where CsUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/?$"
    | where ScStatus == 201
    | project TimeGenerated, CsHost, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, CsUsername, CIp, UserAgent, ScStatus;
// Path 2 — generic ASIM web session table (covers WAF / reverse proxy / API gateway)
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/?$"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname;
union isfuzzy=true AppHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform: identity-swap chain — owner grant followed by login from the granted account Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the full CVE-2026-47413 exploit chain: a successful POST /workspaces/{id}/members with role=owner from caller A, followed within 1 hour by an authentication from a different identity (B) that begins acting on the same workspace from the same source IP. This is the 'second-identity owner' fingerprint the advisory describes. Rationale: Encodes the exploit chain steps 2-4 from the advisory: caller A grants user B owner via POST .../members (201), then within an hour user B authenticates from the same source IP. The same-IP + different-identity within a short window is the specific fingerprint the advisory calls out as hard to attribute via in-app audit logs alone. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8g2p-pqm3-fcfh
ATT&CKT1078 T1098 T1556

[LLM] Vitest UI server launched with non-loopback --api.host / --host (CVE-2026-47429 exposure) Weaponization High
Hunts process creations where node/npm/yarn/pnpm spawns Vitest UI bound to a non-loopback interface via --api.host or --host. Pre-4.1.0 this implicitly grants remote callers file-read and RCE through the /__vitest_attachment__, saveTestFile and rerun APIs. Rationale: Article §Impact lists '--api.host' / api.host config as the precondition for the vulnerability. Pre-extracting the host arg and excluding loopback is the cleanest article-specific filter — every other use of node.exe with vitest is irrelevant. Cross-checked vendor advisory pages and the related GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq (Vitest CSWSH) which confirms the same exposure model. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security • https://vitest.dev/config/api.html
ATT&CKT1574 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "vitest"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ui","--browser")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--api.host","--host","api.host")
| extend HostArg = extract(@"(?i)--(?:api\.)?host(?:[= ])(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(HostArg) and HostArg !in~ ("127.0.0.1","localhost","::1")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, HostArg, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\node.exe", @"\npm.exe", @"\yarn.exe", @"\pnpm.exe", @"\npx.exe")
| where CommandLine has "vitest"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--ui","--browser")
| where CommandLine has_any ("--api.host","--host","api.host")

| where isnotempty(HostArg) and HostArg !in~ ("127.0.0.1","localhost","::1")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, HostArg, ParentProcessName
title: Vitest UI Server Bound to Non-Loopback Interface (CVE-2026-47429)
id: 7b8c2f5e-1d4a-4f2c-9e3b-2a4c6d8e0f1a
description: Detects vitest UI / browser mode invoked with --api.host or --host pointing at a non-loopback interface, exposing the file-read and rerun-RCE APIs to the network.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp
  - https://vitest.dev/config/api.html
author: detection-eng
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1574
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'vitest'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--ui'
      - '--browser'
  selection_host:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--api.host'
      - '--host'
      - 'api.host'
  filter_loopback:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--host=127.0.0.1'
      - '--host 127.0.0.1'
      - '--host=localhost'
      - '--host localhost'
      - '--api.host=127.0.0.1'
      - '--api.host=localhost'
  condition: all of selection_* and not filter_loopback
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\npm.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe)) @CommandLine:(*vitest*) @CommandLine:(*--ui* OR *--browser*) @CommandLine:(*--api.host* OR *--host* OR *api.host*) -@CommandLine:(*localhost* OR *127.0.0.1* OR *::1*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/vitest/i
| CommandLine=/(--ui|--browser)/i
| CommandLine=/(--api\.host|--host|api\.host)/i
| NOT (CommandLine=/(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|::1)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Path-traversal exploit hitting Vitest /__vitest_attachment__ endpoint (CVE-2026-47429 PoC) Exploitation High
Hunts HTTP requests to the Vitest UI server's /__vitest__/ or /__vitest_attachment__ endpoints carrying the Windows-specific '\?\..\' path-traversal payload (or URL-encoded equivalents). This is the literal PoC URL from the advisory bypassing isFileServingAllowed. Rationale: PoC §3 in the advisory uses the literal URL '/__vitest_attachment__?path=...?\..\..\secret.txt'. The '?\..\' sequence is article-specific because the bypass relies on Windows-only quirk (Linux errors on '?' directory). URL-encoded variants %3F%5C..%5C are what curl/browsers send on wire. Cross-checked the vendor advisory and the related Vite CVE-2026-39363 confirming the dev-server-traversal family pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq • https://securityonline.info/vite-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-39364-arbitrary-file-read/
ATT&CKT1190 T1083 T1006
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 51204 or LocalPort == 51204 or RemoteUrl has "__vitest"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(%3F%5C|%3F/|\?\\|\?/)\.\.[\\/]"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: W3C IIS / reverse-proxy logs in front of the Vitest UI host
let TraversalRx = @"(?i)(%3F%5C|%3F/|\?\\|\?/)\.\.[\\/]";
(union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery) matches regex TraversalRx
    | extend Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), SrcIp = cIP, DstHost = Computer, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp, DstHost, sPort, Method, Url, Status, UserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where RequestURL matches regex TraversalRx
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, sPort=DestinationPort, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where Url matches regex TraversalRx
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, sPort=DstPortNumber, Method=HttpMethod, Url, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession"))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Post-exploit shell spawned by Vitest node.exe via rerun / saveTestFile (CVE-2026-47429) Exploitation Medium
Hunts node.exe processes whose command line contains 'vitest' spawning interactive shells, script hosts, or LOLBins. This is the post-exploitation shape when an attacker uses the rerun API to execute attacker-controlled test files written via saveTestFile — equivalent to arbitrary code execution. Rationale: Article §Details: 'it's possible to run arbitrary script by writing a script as a test file using saveTestFile and running it using rerun. This means exposing the API / Vitest UI is equivalent to giving script execution access.' The execution surface is node.exe (the vitest runner) spawning whatever the attacker's malicious test file invokes. Pivoting on parent=node.exe + parent cmdline contains 'vitest' + non-test child binary is the cleanest article-grounded shape. Cross-checked vendor advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "vitest"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","systeminfo.exe","nslookup.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// Reduce FP: vitest legitimately launches node.exe worker children — only flag non-node children
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\cmd.exe",@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe",@"\wscript.exe",@"\cscript.exe",@"\mshta.exe",@"\rundll32.exe",@"\regsvr32.exe",@"\bitsadmin.exe",@"\certutil.exe",@"\curl.exe",@"\wget.exe",@"\whoami.exe",@"\hostname.exe",@"\systeminfo.exe",@"\nslookup.exe")
| where Account !endswith "$"
// Join to a recent vitest invocation on the same host
| join kind=inner (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has "vitest"
    | project VitestTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, VitestPid=NewProcessId, VitestCmd=CommandLine
  ) on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (VitestTime .. VitestTime + 8h)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, VitestCmd

[LLM] Inbound TCP connection to Vitest UI port 51204 from non-loopback source Delivery Medium
Hunts inbound TCP connections to TCP/51204 (Vitest UI default) on endpoints from non-loopback peers — the observable signal that a misconfigured Vitest UI is being reached over the network. Pair with UC1 (the cmdline misconfiguration) for confirmation. Rationale: Article §PoC step 1 uses default 'http://localhost:51204/' — 51204 is Vitest UI's hard-coded default port. Any inbound to that port from non-loopback on a node.exe-driven listener is by definition the exposure path the advisory warns about. Cross-checked the vitest docs and the related GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq advisory which references the same default port. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://vitest.dev/config/api.html • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq
ATT&CKT1133 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort == 51204 and Protocol == "Tcp"
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback" and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1","::1","")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), ConnCount=count(), RemoteIps=make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
          by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen desc
// Sentinel sees this via ASIM ImNetworkSession (or vendor-specific firewall in CommonSecurityLog)
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstPortNumber == 51204 and NetworkProtocol =~ "tcp"
| where DvcAction in~ ("Allow","Allowed","Accept","") or isempty(DvcAction)
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(SrcIpAddr, "127.0.0.0/8"))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sessions=count(), DstHosts=make_set(DstHostname, 20)
          by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstPortNumber
| order by FirstSeen desc

description: Inbound TCP connection accepted on port 51204 (Vitest UI default) from a non-loopback source — the network-side observable of CVE-2026-47429 exposure.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)

| order by conn_count desc

| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Privileged container launch — docker run --privileged from non-CI parent · [LLM] Container escape via cgroups release_agent write (CVE-2022-0492) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Containers on fire: from container escapes to supply chain attacks
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) Command & Control High
Catches the post-compromise C2 beacon from the TeamPCP-poisoned KICS Docker image. Network egress to the hardcoded domain audit.checkmarx.cx or the IP 94.154.172.43 from any host running the tainted KICS scanner container. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP 94.154.172.43 and FQDN audit.checkmarx.cx pre-extracted from the article — the TeamPCP-controlled C2 the KICS stealer talks to during scanning. High-fidelity because these are not generic infrastructure; only an org talking to Checkmarx KICS would even conceivably resolve audit.checkmarx.cx and that domain isn't on any legitimate Checkmarx documentation page (cross-check vs vendor).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic

let bad_domains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (bad_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (bad_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad_ips = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let bad_domains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url

[LLM] Privileged container launch — docker run --privileged from non-CI parent Exploitation Medium
Detects docker / podman / nerdctl invocations carrying --privileged when the parent is not a known container runtime or CI runner. Privileged containers disable nearly all isolation primitives (all capabilities granted, full /dev access, no seccomp) and are the most common pre-condition for container escape in the article. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `--privileged` flag and `docker exec` strings quoted as code blocks in the article. The CI-parent exclusion catches the legitimate use cases (buildkitd, gitlab/jenkins/github runners) and keeps the alert focused on interactive-shell or unexpected-parent invocations, which is where supply-chain compromise or insider misuse shows up.
ATT&CKT1611 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl") or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(docker|podman|nerdctl)\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(ActorUsername in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Container escape via cgroups release_agent write (CVE-2022-0492) Exploitation High
Detects file writes to a release_agent path under /sys/fs/cgroup — the exact primitive abused by CVE-2022-0492 to escape a container and execute arbitrary commands on the host. Pairs the write with the canonical follow-up notify_on_release setting. Rationale: CVE-2022-0492 is explicitly called out in the article as a container-escape vulnerability whose root cause is improper privilege validation on the cgroups release_agent mechanism. The detection anchors on the exact filesystem object the exploit primitive must write to (release_agent + notify_on_release toggle) — there is no benign reason for a containerised workload to touch these files at runtime. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-0492
ATT&CKT1611 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/cgroup/" and (FileName == "release_agent" or FolderPath has "release_agent" or FileName == "notify_on_release")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has "/cgroup/" and (TargetFileName == "release_agent" or TargetFilePath has "release_agent" or TargetFileName == "notify_on_release")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
