[LLM] runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) Installation High
Detects writes to the runC binary on disk by anything other than the legitimate package-manager toolchain. The article calls out CVE-2019-5736 (runC binary overwrite from a compromised container via /proc/self/exe) and CVE-2024-21626 (runC fd handling for host fs access) — both leave the runC executable modified on the node. Rationale: Anchors on the exact runC binary paths and the package-manager exclusion list — CVE-2019-5736 is unique in that successful exploitation requires writing to the host's runC executable from a container context, so any modification of /usr/bin/runc outside the dpkg/yum/snap toolchain is overwhelmingly indicative of either supply-chain compromise or active runC exploit. Also catches the post-exploit cleanup phase of CVE-2024-21626. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-5736 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21626
ATT&CKT1611 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc") or FileName in~ ("runc","docker-runc")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/usr/bin","/usr/sbin","/usr/local/bin","/usr/libexec")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc")
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: runC Binary Modified Outside Package Manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626)
id: 6c0a4b87-1e5f-4d99-aa31-7f2c8b9d3e10
description: Write to the runC executable on disk (/usr/bin/runc, /usr/sbin/runc, /usr/local/bin/runc, docker-runc variants) by a process that is not a known package manager. CVE-2019-5736 abuses /proc/self/exe to overwrite the runC binary from a compromised container; CVE-2024-21626 leaves host artefacts after fd-leak escape.

[LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container Actions on Objectives High
Detects the article's literal curl POST pattern against the Kubernetes API (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/...`) and the canonical ServiceAccount token path. This is exactly the post-compromise behaviour described for the in-container malicious-actions vector — using the mounted /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token to talk to the cluster API. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim Table 2 code block (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H ...`) plus the canonical SA-token path the article explicitly calls out as automatically mounted and attacker-valuable. curl/wget shouldn't be hitting the API server in healthy pods — legitimate workloads use SDKs / kubectl.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1613
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(ParentProcessName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/kubelet'
            - '/kubectl'
            - '/helm'
            - '/argocd'
            - '/flux'
    condition: selection_bin and selection_kube and not filter_parent
falsepositives:
    - In-cluster operators that legitimately curl the API server with their SA token (Prometheus k8s-sd, custom controllers) — allow-list by image/namespace
    - Init containers that probe the API server during pod start-up
level: high

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */wget OR */http OR */httpie) @process.command_line:(*"/api/v1/namespaces"* OR *"/api/v1/pods"* OR *"/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"* OR *"kubernetes.default.svc"* OR *":6443/api/"*) -@process.parent.executable.path:(*/kubelet OR */kubectl OR */helm OR */argocd OR */flux)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(curl|wget|http|httpie)$/i CommandLine=/(\/api\/v1\/(namespaces|pods)|\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes\.io\/serviceaccount\/token|kubernetes\.default\.svc|:6443\/api\/|:8443\/api\/v1\/)/i
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(kubelet|kubectl|helm|argocd|flux)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/eks/<cluster-name>/cluster
fields @timestamp, user.username, sourceIPs, verb, requestURI, userAgent, objectRef.resource, objectRef.namespace, responseStatus.code
| filter userAgent like /^(curl|Wget|HTTPie)/i
      and user.username like /system:serviceaccount:/
      and verb in ["create","get","list","patch","delete","watch"]
| sort @timestamp desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/

date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:

            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 exploit attempt — unauthenticated POST to wpgmp_temp_access_ajax · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 successful exploit — check_temp=false admin-account creation payload
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

[LLM] WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 exploit attempt — unauthenticated POST to wpgmp_temp_access_ajax Exploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php carrying action=wpgmp_temp_access_ajax. The plugin's only intended caller is authenticated support staff; any anonymous traffic to this AJAX action is consistent with the CVE-2026-8732 mass-exploitation Wordfence reported blocking 2,858 of in 24h. Rationale: Article-specific strings used: /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php (the only handler the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook registers), action=wpgmp_temp_access_ajax (the vulnerable action name verbatim from Wordfence's writeup). These two together have effectively zero legitimate unauthenticated POST volume — the feature is for support-staff troubleshooting only. Defender XDR / Falcon FDR / CloudWatch left empty: WordPress access telemetry is webserver/WAF-layer and not in these data sources.
ATT&CKT1190

[LLM] WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 successful exploit — check_temp=false admin-account creation payload Installation High
Hunts the specific exploit payload that triggers unconditional admin-user creation: a POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php containing action=wpgmp_temp_access_ajax with the check_temp=false override. A 200 response means the server returned a magic login URL and wp_insert_user() ran — confirmed successful CVE-2026-8732 exploitation, not just an attempt. Rationale: Article-specific strings: action=wpgmp_temp_access_ajax + check_temp=false — the exact guard-bypass parameter Wordfence identified as the precondition for the unconditional wp_insert_user() call. There is no benign workflow that sends check_temp=false; the parameter exists solely as the access-control bypass. URL-encoded variant (check_temp%3Dfalse) and JSON body variant covered. Status==200 separates confirmed exploitation from blocked attempts. Defender / Falcon / CloudWatch empty: not a host-endpoint or AWS-control-plane detection.
ATT&CKT1068 T1136.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web

| where csUriQuery has "wpgmp_temp_access_ajax"
| where csUriQuery has_any ("check_temp=false", "check_temp%3Dfalse")
| project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Site=sSiteName, ClientIP=cIP, UriStem=csUriStem, UriQuery=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Status=scStatus),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs

| project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Site=tostring(_ResourceId), ClientIP=CIp, UriStem=CsUriStem, UriQuery=CsUriQuery, UA=UserAgent, Status=ScStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestURL has "admin-ajax.php"
| where (RequestURL has "wpgmp_temp_access_ajax" or Message has "wpgmp_temp_access_ajax" or RequestContext has "wpgmp_temp_access_ajax")
| where (RequestURL has "check_temp=false" or Message has "check_temp=false" or RequestContext has "check_temp=false" or Message has "\"check_temp\":false")

[LLM] Post-CVE-2026-8732 hijack — magic-login GET followed by theme/plugin-editor abuse from same IP Actions on Objectives Medium
Correlates the magic-login URL visit (which wp_set_auth_cookie()s the attacker) with subsequent privileged WordPress file-edit endpoints (theme-editor.php / plugin-editor.php / plugin-install.php) from the same client IP within a short window — the article's described post-exploitation behavior for converting admin role into webshell / persistent code execution. Rationale: Article-specific behavior: "returns a magic login URL that, when visited, calls wp_set_auth_cookie() to fully authenticate the attacker as the newly created administrator" → followed by "complete site takeover" (kill-chain phase 7 lists theme-editor.php / plugin-editor.php / unexpected PHP files in wp-content/). Detection joins the CVE-2026-8732 exploit POST (UC1's signature) with WP admin code-edit endpoints from the same IP+site within 1h — the canonical hijack-to-webshell chain. Sigma left empty: multi-event temporal join exceeds single-selection Sigma shape. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch empty: webserver telemetry. FP rate elevated to medium because legitimate admins from VPN-shared IPs can match.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1606.001 T1496
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let lookback = 7d;
let window_sec = 3600;
let WebUnion = (union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | project TimeGenerated, ClientIP=cIP, Site=sSiteName, Method=csMethod, Path=csUriStem, Query=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Status=scStatus),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) | project TimeGenerated, ClientIP=CIp, Site=tostring(_ResourceId), Method=CsMethod, Path=CsUriStem, Query=CsUriQuery, UA=UserAgent, Status=ScStatus),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback) and isnotempty(RequestURL) | project TimeGenerated, ClientIP=SourceIP, Site=DeviceProduct, Method=RequestMethod, Path=tostring(split(RequestURL,"?")[0]), Query=tostring(RequestURL), UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome)));
let Exploits = WebUnion
  | where Method == "POST" and Path endswith "/admin-ajax.php"
  | where Query has "wpgmp_temp_access_ajax"
  | project ExploitTime=TimeGenerated, ClientIP, Site, ExploitQuery=Query;
let PostExpAdmin = WebUnion
  | where Path has_any ("/wp-admin/theme-editor.php","/wp-admin/plugin-editor.php","/wp-admin/plugin-install.php","/wp-admin/update.php")
  | project AdminTime=TimeGenerated, ClientIP, Site, AdminMethod=Method, AdminPath=Path, AdminQuery=Query, UA, Status;
Exploits

| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff("second", AdminTime, ExploitTime)
| where DelaySec between (0 .. window_sec)
| project ExploitTime, AdminTime, DelaySec, ClientIP, Site, ExploitQuery, AdminMethod, AdminPath, AdminQuery, UA, Status
| order by ExploitTime desc

| table firstTime, lastTime, exploit_time, delay_sec, src, dest, methods, paths, count, exploit_count

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

tags:

logsource:
    category: process_creation

detection:

            - '\wscript.exe'

            - '\mshta.exe'

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
